clue.text: Likely to appeal after being shot

definitions.text: Likely to appeal after being shot

parts.words: Likely to appeal after being shot
parts.note: being shot sounds violent, but here it means being photographed: someone who looks good in pictures

explanation.surface: A condemned man hoping his case will go to appeal after a shooting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests gunfire and 'appeal' a court case; the clue really means someone who looks attractive once photographed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who photographs well comes across attractively in pictures taken of them.

clue.text: It isn't all go

definitions.meaning: a piece or portion rather than the whole
to leave or separate, as in to say goodbye and depart

explanation.definitionFit: A portion is less than the whole, and as a verb it means to depart.

clue.text: A pained expression

parts.note: not a grimace on the face but a word said when hurt

explanation.surface: Someone pulls a face in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the exclamation people utter when something suddenly hurts.

clue.text: Traditional cocktail

definitions.meaning: a whisky cocktail with bitters, sugar and orange

explanation.definitionFit: It means outdated or conventional, and is the name of a classic whisky cocktail.

clue.text: Fish always in lake? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: in would put the first piece inside the second
quite the opposite flips the container, so the lake goes inside always instead

parts.note: ever means always
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Is there always a fish in the lake? No, the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' would put EVER inside L, but 'Quite the opposite' turns it round: L goes inside EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An elver is a young eel, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Rude about vessel's prow being on the rocks

indicators.note: about means going around, so the word for rude encloses the letter

parts.note: insolent means rude

indicators.note: the prow is the front of a ship, so take the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An impudent sailor joking about a ship's bow running aground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the rocks' looks like the ship's wreck but means bankrupt; V, the first letter of 'vessel's', goes inside INSOLENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A business on the rocks is failing financially, unable to pay its debts.

clue.text: Went so hurriedly, left without having eaten

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for having eaten goes round the letter

parts.note: having eaten means fed

explanation.surface: Someone rushed off on an empty stomach, leaving before a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means 'outside': FED goes around L.
explanation.definitionFit: To flee is to run away in haste, so the past tense is a hurried departure.

clue.text: A pointless intrigue?

parts.note: pointless evokes a zero score in tennis, and an intrigue is a secret romance

explanation.surface: A scheme that achieves nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A score of nil in tennis is 'love', and an 'affair' is an intrigue.
explanation.definitionFit: A romantic relationship, especially a secret one, is an intrigue of the heart.

clue.text: Given the sack — or let off

definitions.meaning: fired, as a gun is, or released from custody

explanation.definitionFit: It means dismissed from employment, and also fired off or released.

clue.text: From vice I'd reformed in stir, possibly? On the contrary

definitions.text: From vice I'd reformed in stir, possibly? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places the first rearranged group inside the second
possibly says the word stir is only one arrangement of its letters
reformed means formed again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Has a convict given up crime after a spell in prison? Quite the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is slang for prison. The whole clue doubles as the definition: a habitual offender is someone who has emphatically not reformed in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual reoffender keeps returning to crime after being punished, the opposite of going straight.

clue.text: Composer of five symphonies

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is made from part of the following words, running across them

explanation.surface: A trivia question about a composer who wrote five symphonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'fIVE Symphonies'. Charles Ives was an American composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Ives was an American modernist composer, known for orchestral and chamber works.

clue.text: Drag war paint out, becoming less friendly

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Warriors removing their face paint as relations cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people drifting into estrangement grow less close over time.

clue.text: Distinction comic actor got before the war, perhaps

indicators.note: got before puts the actor's name ahead of the next piece

parts.note: Stan Laurel, the comic actor of the duo Laurel and Hardy

indicators.note: perhaps says the words the war are only one possible arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: A comedian won an honour shortly before the outbreak of war.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel was the thin half of the comedy duo Laurel and Hardy; 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange 'the war'.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown of bay leaves was given as an honour to victors and poets, a mark of distinction.

clue.text: Writer's additions? They may be taken out in theatre

definitions.meaning: supplementary sections added at the end of a book

definitions.text: They may be taken out in theatre
definitions.meaning: small organs removed by surgeons in an operating theatre

explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' means an operating theatre, not a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural names both supplements at a book's end and the organs removed in surgery.

clue.text: Two lads get the game started, getting a very good hand

parts.note: Roy is a boy's name
Al is a boy's name
to flush game birds is to drive them from cover

explanation.surface: Two boys starting a game of cards are dealt a superb hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' means birds shot for sport; beaters flush them out.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, ace to ten in one suit is the best possible hand.

clue.text: Not a big audience — it was for charity

definitions.meaning: a theatre with few people in the seats is said to have a thin turnout
a former institution housing paupers at public or charitable expense

explanation.definitionFit: A thin theatre turnout and the old workhouse where paupers lived share this two-word name.

clue.text: Ivan's rule — terrible, in general

indicators.note: terrible suggests the letters are badly jumbled, and nods to Ivan the Terrible

explanation.surface: The tyrant Ivan the Terrible's reign, in general terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Universal means applying to everyone or everything, so broadly general.

clue.text: Thin disc made of iron used in fighting

indicators.note: used in places the metal's symbol inside the word for fighting

parts.note: fighting means war
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A thin metal disc made from iron for use in battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wafer is a thin round biscuit or communion host, a slim disc.

clue.text: Time to finish is what romantic poet may need

parts.note: an era is a period of time
the word to comes as the finish of the answer

explanation.surface: A deadline arrives for a love poet in search of inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Erato is the Greek Muse of love poetry, so a romantic poet needs her inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this Muse presided over lyric and love poetry, inspiring its writers.

clue.text: Substitute in event is showing high concentration

indicators.note: substitute as a verb means swap things around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A substitute coming on in a sporting event shows real focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Substitute' reads as a replacement player, but it is the anagram signal for IN EVENT IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive means concentrated or thorough, as in intensive care or intensive study.

clue.text: The gear demanded by skilled workers?

definitions.text: The gear demanded by skilled workers?

parts.words: The gear demanded by skilled workers?
parts.note: a car's gearing that lets wheels turn at different speeds, and the pay gap skilled workers claim over others

explanation.surface: Craftsmen insisting on the right equipment for the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gear' suggests tools or kit; the clue combines the car part with the extra wage skilled staff demand.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both the axle gear allowing wheels different speeds and a wage gap between grades.

clue.text: Infant raised to do simple arithmetic

parts.note: a tot is a small child
up means raised

explanation.surface: A small child brought up to learn basic sums.
explanation.definitionFit: To add numbers together is the simplest sum, totalling a column.

clue.text: Capital punishment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital punishment' reads as execution but splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: It means excellent, and also a money penalty imposed by a court.

clue.text: Wide smile giving support

definitions.meaning: a horizontal timber or girder holding up a structure

explanation.definitionFit: It is a broad grin and also a timber or girder that bears weight.

clue.text: Vital point in game between numbers of Romans

indicators.note: between places the game inside the pair of numerals

parts.note: C and X are Roman numerals, 100 and 10
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A key moment in a game played between teams of Romans.
explanation.walkthrough: C and X are Roman numerals, 100 and 10; RU (rugby union) goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The crux of a matter is its decisive or central point.

clue.text: Displaying strange antic, pet is like a parrot

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of these words are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: A pet performing an odd trick turns out to behave like a parrot.
explanation.definitionFit: Psittacine is the zoological adjective for parrots and their family.

clue.text: Note goes to small house in London area

parts.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale
ho is a short form of house, small meaning abbreviated

explanation.surface: A message is delivered to a modest home in part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a district of central London known for its nightlife.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district in London's West End.

clue.text: Cutting class to see the race

parts.note: a slip is a cutting taken from a plant
a stream is a school class grouped by ability

explanation.surface: A pupil skips lessons to go and watch a race.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'race' is also the current of air driven back by a propeller; in British schools a 'stream' is an ability group.
explanation.definitionFit: The air thrust backwards by a propeller is called its race, the same airflow behind it.
